Introduction

The MAPT gene, which encodes for tau protein contains three alternatively spliced exons 2, 3 and 10. These give rise to six tau isoforms in adult human brain [9]. Inclusion of the exon 10 leads to the formation of tau protein isoforms with four microtubule binding repeat domains (4R-tau), whereas isoforms with three repeat domains (3R-tau) result from exon 10 exclusion. The isoform composition in brain is developmentally regulated, with only 3R-tau being expressed in foetal brain and roughly similar levels of 3R-and 4R-tau in adult human brain [9]. In the pathological aggregates, the insoluble, fibrillar 3R-and 4R-tau isoform compositions vary distinctively among tauopathies [10,11]. The neurofibrillary tangles (NFTs) in Alzheimer's disease (AD) contain both hyperphosphorylated 3R-and 4R-tau isoforms, whereas insoluble 4R-tau dominates in PSP, cortical basal degeneration (CBD), and argyrophilic grain disease [11,12].
Conversely, Pick bodies, the aggregates in Pick's disease (PiD) contain mainly hyperphosphorylated 3R-tau [11,13,14].

The caudate nucleus in the basal ganglia region is associated with severe tau pathology in PSP brains [27]. In this study, we measured the expression of 3R-and 4R-tau mRNA isoforms and their corresponding protein isoform levels in fifteen PSP cases and neurologically normal controls.
MAPT isoform mRNA
To measure mRNA levels of each MAPT isoform we employed real-time qPCR using
TaqMan chemistry (Applied Biosystems). All transcripts were normalised to the geometric average of three endogenous reference genes and analysed by the delta delta Ct method.

Four-repeat-tau (4R-tau)-transcripts were overexpressed in PSP samples compared to controls with a p-value of 0.02 (Fig. 1a), while no changes were observed in 3R-tau transcript levels between PSP and control (Fig. 1b).
Protein

The 3R-and 4R-tau protein levels in clarified homogenised samples were quantified using the isoform specific 3R-and 4R-tau ELISAs as described previously [24]. The amount of immunoreactive tau was expressed as ng of tau per mg of total brain protein. We observed a significant increase (11.5-fold) in 4R-tau levels in the caudate nucleus of PSP brains compared to control brains (p < 0.05) (Fig. 1c). There was no statistically significant change in 3R-tau levels The median 4R/3R-tau isoform ratio for mRNA expression and combined soluble and insoluble protein levels were found to be 3 and 4.2 respectively (Fig. 2c) Figure 3a).

For 4R-tau, the protein levels ranged from 126 to 1,257 µg per mg of total protein and the 4R mRNA transcript levels ranged from 0.017 to 5.720 (arbitrary units; Figure 3b). We found no statistically significant correlation between the tau protein levels and mRNA expression levels.
The Spearman Rank's correlation coefficient were 0.0715 and 0.0544 for 3R-and 4R-tau, respectively ( Figure. 3a and b).

In this study, we investigated the mRNA and protein levels of 3R-and 4R-tau isoforms in a cohort of PSP cases and aged-matched control samples. Almost a decade ago, Chambers and colleagues used quantitative PCR and first showed increased brainstem 4R-tau mRNA in PSP cases compared to controls [21]. This was also shown in globus pallidus, but not in frontal cortex, a region less severely affected with tau pathology [22,30]. no or weak mRNA-protein correlation [33,34].

In particular, a study of 106 genes in yeast cell found that similar mRNA levels could be accompanied by wide range of protein levels with as much as 30-fold differences and vice versa [34]. Furthermore, a recent study of progranulin (GRN) in frontotemporal lobar  to play an important role in neurodegeration [36], however their effect on tau remains to be elucidated. It is also possible that posttranscriptional changes may be responsible for the lack of correlation between the mRNA and protein levels of progranulin [35] It has been hypothesised that the functions of these regulators include stress response to toxic species, tau inclusions and neuronal death. In addition, the rate of degradation and half-life of tau protein or mRNA in cells as well as transcript turnover rate have not been investigated previously as these could also affect tau mRNA and protein correlation.

The pH of brains and postmortem delay most certainly affect the quality and levels of mRNA and proteins [37]. In this study, both protein and mRNA were extracted and processed simultaneously from the same piece of brain tissue to exclude possible bias.

conclusion

To our knowledge, this is the first study in PSP in which the levels of 3R-and 4R-tau isoforms both at the mRNA and protein levels were investigated. We have confirmed previous findings showing the specific increase in 4R-tau isoforms in an affected region of the PSP brain compared to controls and showed that this increase is reflected also at the protein level. We also observed an overall correlation between protein and mRNA expression between PSP and controls in the brain region with tau pathology.

supranuclear palsy (PSP, MIM 601104; Steele-Richardson-Olszewski Syndrome) [1] is a sporadic neurodegenerative disorder of late adult life. It is the second most common form of parkinsonism and is clinically characterised by an akinetic-rigid syndrome, supranuclear down gaze palsy, pseudobulbar signs and cognitive decline of frontal lobe type [2-4]. Pathologically, PSP belongs to a group of neurodegenerative diseases called tauopathies that are defined by the presence of insoluble tau protein aggregates in brain ( [5] for reviews see [6-8]). Tau protein is an axonal component that maintains and stabilises the neuronal network by binding to the microtubules along the axon via its carboxy-terminal domain.

Our results showed that there is an overall increase in total (soluble and insoluble) 4R-tau levels (614,148±337,648 ng of tau per mg of total protein) compared to total 3R-tau levels (226,139±194,596 ng of tau per mg of total protein) in 18 PSP cases (p<0.05) (Figure 2a). Our results are in line with these findings showing about a three-fold increase in 4R-tau:3R-tau ratio in PSP patients. This indicates that the increase in 4R-tau and 4R-tau:3R-tau mRNA ratio is an important process associated with, if not directly contributing to PSP pathogenesis. This is clearly the case with those FTDP-17 cases with MAPT exon 10 splice-site mutations that effect increased 4R-tau mRNA due to increased inclusion of exon 10. This study shows that the overall tau protein levels correspond to the mRNA levels as increases in both tau immunoreactivity and mRNA levels were observed in the caudate nucleus region of PSP brains compared to control brains. As expected, we also show that the insoluble tau fraction isolated by highspeed centrifugation consists almost exclusively of 4R-tau isoforms. This is the first direct measurement of tau isoforms from the pathological inclusions and confirms the neuropathological and biochemical classification of PSP as a four-repeat tauopathy [10, 11, 31, 32]. In previous studies, we also showed increased pathological 4R-tau burden in regions associated with pathology [24, 27] 4.1. Messenger RNA-protein correlations We also compared the amount of mRNA transcripts against the combined soluble and insoluble tau isoforms within each sample to determine if there is a direct correlation between mRNA levels and protein levels. Regression analysis did not show a significant correlation between individual protein values and their corresponding mRNA levels for either 3R or 4R, although a positive line of best fit between the two variables was obtained for both isoforms. These results are not so surprising when we consider the number of different mechanisms that affect mRNA and protein turnover. In particular, real-time qPCR mRNA quantitation relies on normalization against a choice of reference normalising genes with the assumption that these genes have similar expression levels in different brain regions and independent of disease state. However, most genes have regional and disease-specific expression differences and this requires careful reference gene assessment and data analysis. In order to minimise this effect, we used the geometric mean of three normalizing genes commonly used in qPCR expression studies in human brain. With the rapid development of high-throughput proteomics and array-based mRNA analysis it is possible that we will soon have more robust and accurate means of assessing mRNA species and proteins with extensive posttranslational modifications for more reliable mRNA-protein correlation studies. However, we believe that with our ELISAs, the quantitation of the insoluble tau fraction after solubilisation with guanidium hydrochloride provides a reasonably accurate measure of levels of tau from the inclusions due to the unmasking of the antibody epitopes.

Previous studies have shown that mRNA levels rarely correlate with the corresponding protein. It would therefore be important to ascertain the post-transcriptional and post-translational events that determine tau isoform levels, defects of which lead to the abnormal, isoform-specific sequestration of the hyperphosphorylated tau in the pathological inclusions. This would be of particular importance for the understanding of the role of genetic risk factors and how they ultimately manifest as changes in tau isoforms.

RNA integrity was assessed by the presence of distinct ribosomal RNA 18S and 28S bands on denaturing formaldehyde agarose gels stained with ethidium bromide. One microgram of extracted RNA was transformed into cDNA using SuperScript III First-Strand Synthesis SuperMix for qRT-PCR (Invitrogen). The 3R-and 4R-tau transcripts were measured as described previously[26]. Beta-actin, GAPDH, and HPRT were used as endogenous controls (Applied Biosystems). All samples were run in triplicates.Fluorescence was detected using the Stratagene Mx3000P qPCR system. All samples were analysed using the delta-delta Ct method.2.5. Data analysisGraphPad Prism software was used for statistical analysis. Data to compare control and PSP samples as well as data comparing 4R-and 3R-tau levels with unequal variances were analysed using unpaired-T test with Welch's corrections. The relationships between tau mRNA and protein levels within each sample were analysed using Spearman's rank coefficient correlation and logistic regressions.
